solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rising priest meets old officer

blocks.note: Rev is the short form of Reverend, a title for a priest
O is a standard abbreviation for old
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A clergyman on his way up encounters a retired officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like it describes the priest, but it is the definition, in the sense of an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is a popular rebellion, so the noun is a synonym of revolt.

clue.text: Wariness about African politicians in unusual cult close to questionable

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters are set in a new order
'close to' keeps only the last letter of 'questionable'

blocks.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party
taken as written
the final letter of questionable

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of African politicians joining a strange sect.
explanation.walkthrough: The politicians go in among the letters of cult, and the whole group is rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctance is hesitancy or unwillingness, close in meaning to being wary.

clue.text: Artist showing fruit without marks in very good hotel

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the fruit
in places what remains of the fruit inside the hotel description

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
a tropical fruit
M stands for marks, the old German currency
G is the abbreviation for good
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A painter displays an unblemished piece of fruit at a fine hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without marks' suggests unblemished fruit, but marks is the German currency, abbreviated M, removed from MANGO; ANGO then sits inside V G H.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent van Gogh was the Dutch post-impressionist painter of Sunflowers.

clue.text: Liberal sun in Cornish resort

indicators.note: in places one element inside the resort's name

blocks.note: Looe is a fishing town and resort in Cornwall
S is the abbreviation for sun, or Sunday

explanation.surface: A permissive attitude to sunbathing at a seaside town in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose and liberal both mean free or not strict, as in a loose translation.

clue.text: Prank ceased possibly with intervention of old man

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word could be arranged another way
something that intervenes comes between, so it is placed inside

blocks.note: taken as written
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A practical joke stopped, perhaps because an elderly man stepped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is a crossword staple for a father, here PA.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure, much like a prank.

clue.text: One with crook viewed endless food

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a shepherd carries a crook, a hooked staff
spied means saw

explanation.surface: Someone holding a crook was watched eating forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' suggests a criminal, but it is a shepherd's staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's pie is a British dish of minced lamb topped with mashed potato.

clue.text: A bachelor blocking Balkan in charge of a circus performer?

indicators.note: to block something is to stand in its way, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a Croat is a native of Croatia, a Balkan state
B is the abbreviation for bachelor
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A single man obstructing a Balkan who runs a circus act.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the end phrase read as an adjective phrase; the question mark admits that tumbling is only one sort of circus act.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatic describes the agile tumbling and balancing done by a circus acrobat.

clue.text: Feature of dish enabling woman to retain figure?

indicators.note: to retain something is to hold it within

blocks.note: a woman's name
a number, or figure

explanation.surface: A dish that helps a woman keep her figure, as if a diet meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' suggests food and 'figure' a slim body, but the dish is a satellite dish and the figure a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite dish has an antenna, the part that picks up the broadcast signal.

clue.text: Comfort in coffee as expected

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of coffee, all of as and the start of expected

explanation.surface: A cup of coffee is as soothing as one would hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of relaxation and freedom from pain, much like comfort.

clue.text: US writer snubbed single academic fellow

indicators.note: snubbed puns on snub-nosed, cut short, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: lone means single, solitary
a don is a university fellow or tutor

explanation.surface: An American author cold-shouldered an unmarried university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' reads as ignored, but it means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London was the American novelist who wrote The Call of the Wild.

clue.text: Rubbish I trusted to be shifted

indicators.note: shifted letters are moved around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Junk I had relied on now needs moving out.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or waste matter left behind, so it is a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Manager in juniors' home ground gathering ball

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, as in a mill, so the letters are broken and remixed

blocks.note: taken as written
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A football manager at the youth team's stadium collecting a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a football stadium but signals the anagram; 'gathering' just adds the ball to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Mourinho is the Portuguese football manager known for spells at Chelsea, Real Madrid and Manchester United.

clue.text: Almost offensive like an intense osteologist?

blocks.note: first meaning: near the limit of decency, risqué
second meaning, read literally: someone studying bones very closely

explanation.surface: A joke nearly crosses the line, like a bone scientist peering hard at a specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: An osteologist studies bones; the question mark flags the literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes remarks that are near the knuckle, verging on rude or hurtful.

clue.text: Unadventurous talk almost in host team before playing

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
playing suggests letters at play, moving about into new positions

blocks.note: to yak is to chatter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dull chatter among the home side ahead of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened chatter goes in with the host team's letters before they are all rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay-at-home person prefers familiar surroundings to travel or risk, so lacks a sense of adventure.

clue.text: Jumper, say, left among articles, extremely threadbare

indicators.note: among places one letter in the midst of the others
extremely points to the two extremities of the word, its ends

blocks.note: A and THE, the indefinite and definite articles
L is the abbreviation for left
the first and last letters of threadbare

explanation.surface: A sweater, perhaps, abandoned among old items, worn very thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a British sweater, but it is a high or long jumper; L goes between the H and E of the articles.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper in track and field is one kind of sportsperson, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Marker of collapsed crust?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that marks a pie whose pastry has caved in
setter's reading: the earth's crust giving way in an earthquake, whose surface point is marked

explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture of a failed pie hides geology: the crust is the earth's outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake.

clue.text: Withdraw spiritual booklet?

blocks.note: RE is religious education, the school subject
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: Taking back a religious pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for religious education, a British school subject; the question mark covers that loose link to spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement or a claw is to take it back or pull it in.

clue.text: Cafe's beginning observable line mostly in foreign meat

indicators.note: beginning points to the opening letter only
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the first letter of cafe
the horizon is the line where earth and sky appear to meet

explanation.surface: A cafe begins serving a mostly visible line of imported sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorizo is a spicy Spanish pork sausage, an example of meat from abroad.

clue.text: New policy in North thrown out? There's great applause

indicators.note: thrown out means ejected, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: an innovation is a new method or idea
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A fresh policy in the North is rejected, yet people cheer loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of what goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a sustained burst of clapping, often a standing one.

clue.text: Recourse for those with complaints?

blocks.note: surface reading: where aggrieved customers go to grumble
setter's reading: complaints are ailments, so the place is where the ill are treated

explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaints' suggests grievances, but it means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick bay is a room on a ship or in a school where ill people are cared for.

clue.text: Rustic fruit given different cover

indicators.note: a new cover is a fresh outside, so the front letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: a large orange gourd

explanation.surface: A country-style gourd wrapped in a new skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The cover is the first letter: P becomes B, and nothing in the clue says which letter, so crossers settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpkin is an unsophisticated country person, a rustic used as a noun.

clue.text: Long-standing envoy, say, represented maladroit creep

indicators.note: represented means presented anew, so the letters are put in a different form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran ambassador is portrayed as a clumsy toady.
explanation.definitionFit: A career diplomat is a professional in the foreign service, not a political appointee; an envoy is one example.

clue.text: Scream in US city, repugnant sound

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
ugh is the noise of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone in an American city shrieks with revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scream' suggests terror, but here it is a noun for something hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a scream and a laugh both mean a very funny person or thing.

clue.text: Precious stuff round china

blocks.note: O is round in shape
china is rhyming slang: china plate = mate, a pal

explanation.surface: Valuable material surrounding a piece of porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' suggests porcelain, but in Cockney rhyming slang it means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone, a precious material prized for its play of colour.

clue.text: Artistic work, popular element in retrospective opening

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word is read backwards
in puts the joined pieces inside the turned-round word

blocks.note: a gap is an opening
in means fashionable, popular
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A well-liked piece at the opening of an artist's retrospective exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective' looks like an art exhibition, fitting the surface, but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting is a picture made with paint, one kind of artistic work.

clue.text: Daft flier?

blocks.note: first meaning: crazy, silly
second meaning: a bird famed for its call and laying eggs in others' nests

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it is a foolish bird; the question mark marks the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is slang for mad, and also the name of a common migrant bird.

clue.text: Knight from county set with son going to Spain

indicators.note: going to means turning into, so one letter becomes another

blocks.note: Lancs is the short form of Lancashire, an English county
S is the abbreviation for son
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a lot is a set or group of items

explanation.surface: A knight comes from an English county, and his boy travels to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; the S at its end is swapped for Spain's code E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the most famous Knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: What's turning point after Western protest?

indicators.note: after says the turning point is placed second, following the western abbreviation

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
a hinge is the point on which a door turns

explanation.surface: Someone asks what pivotal moment followed a protest in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning point' suggests a decisive moment, but here it is literally a pivot.
explanation.definitionFit: To whinge is British slang for complain peevishly, a grumbling form of protest.
